title: A norm-pair geometric witness from a single simple orbit zero
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $D$ be a smooth proper integral finite-type $k$-scheme of dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $G$ be a finite group acting by $k$-automorphisms on $D$ and let $x$ be a $k$-rational closed point for which the points $gx$ are distinct. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_D$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], let $n\geq1$ and suppose $L^{\otimes n}$ is generated by global sections [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections]. Let $a\in H=\Gamma(D,L^{\otimes n})$ have a simple zero at $x$ (in any local frame its coefficient belongs to $\mathfrak m_x\setminus\mathfrak m_x^2$) and be nonzero at all $gx$ for $g\ne1$. Use [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-sfb-pencil-orbit-bundle-norm] to put $B=\bigotimes_{g\in G}g^*L$ and $\mathcal N_G(c)=\bigotimes_{g\in G}g^*c\in\Gamma(D,B^{\otimes n})$ for $c\in H$. Write $Z(a)$ for the points where the residue-field value of $a$ is zero, and put $S=\bigcup_{g\in G}g^{-1}Z(a)$. Then $S$ is a finite $G$-stable set of $k$-rational closed points, $H$ is finite-dimensional, and evaluation at each $y\in S$ has a proper kernel in $H$. There exists $b\in H$ nonzero at every point of $S$. For any such $b$, putting $s=\mathcal N_G(a)$ and $t=\mathcal N_G(b)$, one has $Z(s)=S$, $s,t$ have no common zero and generate $B^{\otimes n}$. Moreover in any local frame of $B^{\otimes n}$ near $x$, if $s=\alpha e$ and $t=\beta e$, then $\alpha\in\mathfrak m_x\setminus\mathfrak m_x^2$, $\beta$ is a unit, and $d(\alpha/\beta)$ has nonzero value in $\Omega^1_{D/k}\otimes\kappa(x)$, where $\Omega^1_{D/k}$ is the relative differential sheaf [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] and $d$ is the universal Kähler derivation [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. No division by $|G|$ or restriction on $\operatorname{char}k$ is involved.

proof.text: Put $M=L^{\otimes n}$. Tensoring local rank-one frames shows that $M$ is invertible. Apply the proper-field invertible-coherence lemma to $(D,M)$: $D$ is Noetherian and $M$ is coherent. Proper coherent cohomology finiteness, in degree zero, gives $H=\Gamma(D,M)$ finite-dimensional over $k$ (degree-zero cohomology is global sections). No ampleness or projectivity is assumed in either application.

source.place: Tag 01XZ, lemma-coherent-Noetherian; Tag 02O5, proposition-proper-pushforward-coherent, field base, degree zero

proof.text: The germ of $a$ at $x$ is nonzero because its coefficient is not in $\mathfrak m_x^2$, so $a\ne0$. The nonzero-section Cartier lemma applies to the integral scheme $D$ and the invertible module $M$. Write $E=Z_{\mathrm{sch}}(a)$ for its effective Cartier zero scheme. On a trivializing affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, with $a=c e$, it is cut out by $(c)$, so its underlying closed set is exactly the residue-field zero set $Z(a)$ in the question. The scheme-dimension lemma identifies the topological Krull dimension $1$ of $D$ with $\sup_{y\in D}\dim\mathcal O_{D,y}$, so $\dim D\le1$ in the local-ring sense required by the Cartier-divisor finiteness lemma. Since $D$ is proper, that lemma gives $\dim E\le0$ (local-ring sense) and every point closed in $E$.

source.place: Tag 02OR, lemma-zero-scheme (3)-(4), with the integral-section lemma; varieties.tex Tag 0AYY, lemma-degree-effective-Cartier-divisor, first proof sentences

proof.text: The closed subset $|E|$ of the Noetherian scheme $D$ is a union of finitely many irreducible components by the cited finite-components lemma. Each such component has at most one point: otherwise a closed singleton properly contained in that irreducible closed component would be a chain of irreducible closed subsets of length one, contradicting $\dim E\le0$, which by the scheme-dimension lemma applied to the scheme $E$ is also its topological Krull dimension. Thus $Z(a)$ is finite. Its points are closed in $D$ because $E$ is closed. The closed-point residue-field lemma applies to the finite-type $k$-scheme $D$ and algebraically closed $k$, making all of these points $k$-rational.

source.place: Tag 0BA8, lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components, applied to the closed subspace; algebra.tex Tag 00FV and morphisms.tex Tag 01TB for closed-point residue fields

proof.text: The set $S=\bigcup_{g\in G}g^{-1}Z(a)$ is finite since $G$ and $Z(a)$ are finite. Every $g$ is a $k$-automorphism, so inverse images of closed $k$-rational points are closed $k$-rational points. For $h\in G$ and $y\in S$, choose $g$ with $gy\in Z(a)$; then $(gh^{-1})(hy)=gy\in Z(a)$, whence $hy\in S$. Applying this also to $h^{-1}$ proves $hS=S$. In particular $x\in S$ because $a(x)=0$.

source.place: Agent finite-orbit set computation supporting Tag 0C1E, lemma-uniformizer-works; the norm-pair construction of this item

proof.text: For each $y\in S$, evaluation $\operatorname{ev}_y:H\to M\otimes\kappa(y)$ is $k$-linear. If it were zero, every global section would have germ in $\mathfrak m_yM_y$. Global generation says that a local frame of $M$ is locally a finite sum of functions times global sections. Taking germs at $y$ and reducing modulo $\mathfrak m_y$ would express its nonzero residue as a sum of zeros, a contradiction. Consequently $\ker(\operatorname{ev}_y)$ is a proper linear subspace of $H$.

source.place: Tag 01AM, definition-globally-generated, expanded in a local rank-one frame

proof.text: The field $k$ is infinite: if its elements formed a finite set, the nonconstant polynomial $\prod_{c\in k}(T-c)-1$ would have no root in $k$, contradicting algebraic closedness. Apply finite linear avoidance to the finite-dimensional $k$-space $H$ and the finite family of proper subspaces $\ker(\operatorname{ev}_y)$, indexed by $y\in S$. It yields $b\in H$ outside their union, exactly a section nonzero at every point of $S$.

source.place: Finite linear avoidance; agent polynomial argument for infinitude from the definition of algebraic closedness

proof.text: Fix any such $b$. For each point $y$ choose frames of $L$ near the finitely many $gy$, pull them back, take tensor powers and their ordered tensor product, and apply the comparison defining the norm. On the intersection of their inverse-image neighbourhoods this is a frame of $B^{\otimes n}$. If $c_g$ is the local coefficient of $g^*c$, the coefficient of $\mathcal N_G(c)$ is $\prod_{g\in G}c_g$. Indeed pullback sends a section coefficient to its image under $g^\sharp$, and tensoring pure sections multiplies their coefficients; induction over the finite list in the norm definition gives the formula. The residue of $c_g$ at $y$ is zero precisely when $c(gy)=0$, since a $k$-automorphism induces an isomorphism of residue fields. A finite product in a field is zero precisely when some factor is zero. Applying this to $c=a$ proves $Z(s)=S$.

source.place: Tag 01AM, definition-globally-generated; local rank-one unit calculation

proof.text: At $x$, use the product frame from step 7. The identity factor for $a$ has coefficient in $\mathfrak m_x\setminus\mathfrak m_x^2$ by hypothesis. Every other factor has unit coefficient because $a(gx)\ne0$ for $g\ne1$. Thus the coefficient of $s$ is this identity coefficient multiplied by a unit. All factors for $b$ are units since the orbit of $x$ lies in $S$, so the coefficient of $t$ is a unit. Changing to any frame $e$ multiplies both coefficients by the same unit; therefore $s=\alpha e$, $t=\beta e$ satisfy $\alpha\in\mathfrak m_x\setminus\mathfrak m_x^2$ and $\beta\in\mathcal O_{D,x}^{\times}$. Multiplication by a unit preserves both $\mathfrak m_x$ and $\mathfrak m_x^2$, so $q=\alpha/\beta$ also lies in $\mathfrak m_x\setminus\mathfrak m_x^2$.

source.place: Agent one-simple-factor product calculation preceding the application of Tag 0C1E, lemma-uniformizer-works

proof.text: Put $R=\mathcal O_{D,x}$. Properness implies separatedness, and the scheme-dimension lemma turns the topological dimension one of $D$ into $\sup_{y}\dim\mathcal O_{D,y}=1$, so $D$ is a separated integral finite-type curve in the sense of the curve definition; smoothness and the closed-stalk structure lemma show that $R$ is Noetherian. Its residue field is $k$ by the given rationality of $x$, hence is a finitely generated separable extension of $k$. The cotangent-injectivity lemma sends the nonzero class of $q$ in $\mathfrak m_x/\mathfrak m_x^2$ to $dq\otimes1\ne0$ in $\Omega_{R/k}\otimes_R k$. To read this in the sheaf appearing in the conclusion, take the smooth (hence locally finitely presented) affine chart supplied by the affine-chart stalk-differentials lemma, with base $\operatorname{Spec}k$. It identifies $\Omega^1_{D/k,x}$ with the localization of the chart's algebraic differentials, compatibly with $d$. Differential localization then identifies that localization with $\Omega_{R/k}$ and sends each $df/u$ to $u^{-1}d(f/1)$. Tensoring these inverse isomorphisms with $k$ carries $dq\otimes1$ to the value of $d(\alpha/\beta)$ in $\Omega^1_{D/k}\otimes\kappa(x)$, so this value is nonzero. All products and local inverses above are defined in every characteristic; none uses $|G|^{-1}$.
